GoatDB: The Realtime State Layer for Human-Agent Collaboration

GoatDB is the realtime state layer for human-agent collaboration: humans, AI agents, tools, and devices share the same live, durable state. Under the hood it is an embedded, distributed document database providing verifiable local-first state continuity, prioritizing speed, developer experience, and signed provenance.

Instead of following traditional database design patterns, GoatDB leverages concepts refined over decades by distributed version control systems. In secure mode (default), every write produces a cryptographically signed commit appended to a durable commit graph. Concurrent changes merge deterministically through Git-style three-way merge at the field level. The commit graph is the authoritative source of repository state — not the network, server, or any single peer.

Currently optimized for TypeScript environments, GoatDB functions as a first-class citizen in both browsers and servers. It utilizes a document model with schemas, providing causal eventual consistency to simplify development while offering built-in Ed25519 session signing (default secure mode) for the underlying commit graph.

Core Features:
- Durable Commit Graph: Append-only source of truth for repository state; cryptographically signed in secure mode (default)
- Repository-Centric Design: Independent units of data synchronization and access control
- Memory-First Architecture: Explicit control with predictable performance
- Local Query Processing: Reactive query engine with distributed consistency
- Deterministic Structural Merge: Git-style three-way merge at the field level
- Signed Provenance: Ed25519 session signatures on every commit (default secure mode)
- Server Recovery: Any authorized client replica holding the relevant history can restore a crashed server
- Offline-First: Full local replicas of each opened repository; work continues without network connectivity

Current Network Architecture:
- Carrier: HTTP (current); WebSocket and WebRTC planned
- Trigger: Polling with 200ms scheduler checks plus per-repository adaptive 300–1500ms cycles
- Typical latency: 700–1000ms application-perceived
- Topology: Server-coordinated (current); direct P2P via WebRTC planned
- Sync protocol: Transport-independent, delta-compressed, Bloom-filter-based reconciliation
